record.paper_title: Neutrino-nucleus interactions: open questions and future projects
record.original_question: How can the unknown quantity L1,A in neutrino-deuteron reaction theory be determined, and how would determining L1,A improve the precision of calculations relevant to the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory deuteron detector response and to the solar proton-proton reaction?

evidence.quote: The best known case is the neutrino-deuteron reaction, relevant for the SNO experiment [16], where theoretical calculations reach the few percent precision [17]. However, there is still an important unknown quantity L1,A whose determination would improve our knowledge of the pp reaction in the Sun.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In pionless effective field theory descriptions of low-energy neutrino–deuteron reactions (charged-current and neutral-current breakup, as well as elastic neutrino–deuteron scattering), the dominant theoretical uncertainty for all weak two-nucleon processes at the relevant energies can be absorbed into a single isovector axial two-body counterterm, denoted L_{1,A} (with dimensions of fm^3), which parameterizes the strength of the axial two-body current at the leading order at which it appears. The same counterterm enters the calculation of the proton–proton fusion rate p+p → d + e^+ + ν_e, which sets the solar pp luminosity, and the neutrino–deuteron cross sections used to interpret the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory (SNO) detector response.

Problem. (a) Devise a method—using experimental data (e.g., reactor antineutrino–deuteron breakup, solar neutrino data from SNO, tritium β-decay, muon capture on the deuteron) and/or first-principles calculations (e.g., lattice QCD or chiral effective field theory matching)—that determines the numerical value of L_{1,A} to a precision sufficient to reduce the theoretical uncertainty in the neutrino–deuteron breakup cross sections below the 1% level over the SNO energy range. (b) Quantify how a precise determination of L_{1,A} propagates into the theoretical uncertainty of the astrophysical S-factor S_{pp}(0) of the proton–proton fusion reaction in the Sun.
artifact.category_tag: Effective field theory of weak nuclear currents
artifact.status_search_result: L_{1,A} has been constrained by multiple methods (reactor antineutrino–deuteron data, SNO data, solar luminosity+helioseismology, tritium β-decay, and lattice QCD). A 2019/2020 analysis (Baroni et al., Phys. Rev. C 101, 015505) provided a new determination L_{1,A} ≈ 4.9^{+1.9}_{-1.5} fm^3 (at μ = m_π), consistent with prior experimental constraints and a recent lattice QCD calculation. However, the precision remains at the few-percent level for SNO-relevant cross sections, so the goal of sub-percent precision motivating dedicated experiments has not been fully achieved; thus the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Neutrino-deuteron scattering: Uncertainty quantification and new L_{1,A} constraints
status_evidence.snippet: New determination of L_{1,A} with uncertainty quantification, giving L_{1,A} ≈ 4.9^{+1.9}_{-1.5} fm^3, compatible with previous experimental determinations and lattice QCD.
status_evidence.claim: L_{1,A} has been constrained but with residual uncertainty of order 30–40%, leading to several-percent uncertainty in SNO-relevant cross sections.

status_evidence.title: Elastic and inelastic neutrino-deuteron scattering in effective field theory
status_evidence.snippet: Pionless EFT treatment of νd reactions identifying L_{1,A} as the dominant unknown two-body axial counterterm.
status_evidence.claim: L_{1,A} is the single axial two-body counterterm controlling theoretical uncertainty in νd reactions.
